newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela wage hike said to impact inflation 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela wage hike said to impact inflation 5 pct.

text.p: The inflationary impact of the expected increase in Venezuela's minimum wage will be around five percent, a top Central Bank official said Tuesday.
The planned raise will translate into "an inflation boost of between 4.5 and 5.5 percent," the bank's first vice-president Hugo Romero Quintero told reporters.

Venezuela's minimum wage is due to be increased as soon as Congress approves a complex severance pay reform bill, which it is now studying. Romero said strong fiscal discipline would likely lessen the inflationary impact of the popular measure.

Government officials have said the minimum salary will be increased to between 62,000 bolivars ($130) and 75,000 bolivars ($157) from the current urban level of 53,000 bolivars, including bonuses. The country's largest trade union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), has asked for 90,000 bolivars ($189).
Inflation, at a record 103 percent in 1996, is sharply going down in Venezuela and came in at 1.6 percent in March, the lowest level in five years. The official 1997 target is 35 percent.
